content_html:
I recently saw complaints about Google’s search engine crawler taking down websites by sending them too much traffic:

We had googlebot blast a random customer system and almost cause an outage, this is when I first learnt that google will use it for AI training also. It's honestly kind of frustrating also because you then search on it and theres (was) nothing on how you are meant to "correctly" tell google to fuck off, and not use it like that.

— User jofzar on Hacker News

Google's web scraping functionality has been acting as a ddos for more than two decades. I've seen literally hundreds of reports of them attacking websites and taking them down, where there's nothing you can do but accept the traffic, or get delisted

— User 20k on Hacker News

But I think these complaints are misguided. This traffic doesn’t come from Google at all. It comes from other people’s bots impersonating Googlebot’s name for misleading and arguably-abusive purposes.

Most* Googlebots are fake.

The user agent header is a pinky promise

When people say that they see traffic from Googlebot, they usually mean that they see Googlebot in the user agent header, usually embedded in a string like this:

User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1; +http://www.google.com/bot.html)

Or, if you’re looking at nginx-style server logs, it might look something like this:

78.142.228.252 - - [17/Jul/2026:14:57:44 +0000] "GET /blog HTTP/1.1" 200 4821 "-" "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1; +http://www.google.com/bot.html)"

This is all fine and dandy, but this header doesn’t mean it’s the real Googlebot at all. The user agent is a voluntary self-identification. Anyone making an HTTP request can set that user agent value to anything!

On the internet, no one knows you’re a dog… and the flip side is that I can claim to be a dog (or a Googlebot) whenever I feel like it.

These liars impersonate Googlebot in hopes that it will help them bypass bot controls; indeed, if you look up that IP in my log above, it comes from Virtual Machine Solutions LLC. This is a hosting provider, so someone (not Google) rented a server from them to send this traffic.

People do this, all the time, and it seems to have hit a new scale recently. Chris Siebenmann theorizes that “it’s a large scale campaign by a single abusive crawler by people who can afford to obtain a lot of servers at a lot of different hosting providers”, rather than a widespread rise in popularity for an old trick.

Lightning Q&A

Q: How do I verify that a request came from the real Googlebot?

A: Here are Google’s docs for verifying Googlebot; in short, you can spot-check with a couple of `host` commands or check against Google’s published IP ranges. Most major crawlers publish some kind of IP list, but the details vary; the JAFAR proposal aims to standardize these lists, though it’s still working its way through the standard-making process.

Q: What if I looked up the IP address and saw it was registered to Google LLC?

A: I’d still run through the verification process, since “Google LLC” is also the registration for Google Cloud hosting IP addresses. Though personally, I wasn’t able to find any recent examples of this - I wouldn’t be surprised if the Google Cloud anti-abuse team had some kind of controls to crack down on this.

Q: I checked and it really is real Googlebot. What should I do?

A: See Google’s docs on how to handle overcrawling of your site.

Q: You mean to tell me people can lie on the internet?

A: Yes :(

Q: What if we added another field to stop them from lying?

A: Please refer to RFC 3514, the “evil bit” standard. Unfortunately, bad actors do not comply with this standard.

On a more serious note, I’ve written at length about the Web Bot Auth HTTP Signatures proposal for my employer (as always, opinions on this blog my own). That proposal is a little more complicated than just another field since it involves a cryptographic signature, but I think it’s a reasonable path to “a user agent you can trust”.

*Q: You’ve convinced me some Googlebots are fake. But is it really “most”?

A: Okay, I concede that I don’t have data to prove this. I offer this weaker claim: most stories of disruptive Googlebot traffic (like the quotes at the start of this post) are caused by fake Googlebots. In my experience, the real Googlebot is very well-behaved; meanwhile, fake Googlebots are happy to hammer on a site until it explodes.

That being said, if you have seen disruptive behavior from Googlebots (real or fake), I’d like to hear about it - reach out at bobbie@digitalseams.com.

content_html_zh:
我最近看到有关谷歌搜索引擎爬虫程序因向网站发送过多流量而导致网站瘫痪的投诉：

我们让 googlebot 随机攻击了一个客户系统，几乎导致了停机，这是我第一次了解到 google 也将使用它进行人工智能训练。 老实说，这也有点令人沮丧，因为你随后搜索它，却没有任何关于你如何“正确”告诉谷歌滚蛋，而不是那样使用它的内容。 — Hacker News 上的用户 jofzar 二十多年来，Google 的网络抓取功能一直充当 DDoS 攻击。 我确实看到过数百份关于他们攻击网站并将其关闭的报告，除了接受流量或被除名之外，您别无选择 — Hacker News 上的用户 20k

但我认为这些抱怨是误导性的。 这些流量根本不是来自谷歌。 它来自其他人的机器人冒充 Googlebot 的名字，以达到误导和可能滥用的目的。

大多数* Googlebot 都是假的。

用户代理标头是一个小指承诺

当人们说他们看到来自 Googlebot 的流量时，他们通常意味着他们在用户代理标头中看到 Googlebot，通常嵌入在如下字符串中：

用户代理：Mozilla/5.0（兼容；Googlebot/2.​​1；+http://www.google.com/bot.html）

或者，如果您正在查看 nginx 风格的服务器日志，它可能看起来像这样：

78.142.228.252 - - [17/Jul/2026:14:57:44 +0000]“GET /blog HTTP/1.1”200 4821“-”“Mozilla/5.0（兼容；Googlebot/2.​​1；+http://www.google.com/bot.html）”

这一切都很好，但这个标题并不意味着它是真正的 Googlebot。 用户代理是自愿的自我标识。 任何发出 HTTP 请求的人都可以将该用户代理值设置为任何值！

在互联网上，没有人知道你是一只狗...... 另一方面是，只要我愿意，我就可以声称自己是一只狗（或谷歌机器人）。

这些骗子冒充 Googlebot，希望能帮助他们绕过机器人控制；事实上，如果您在我上面的日志中查找该 IP，它来自 Virtual Machine Solutions LLC。 这是一个托管提供商，因此有人（不是 Google）从他们那里租用了服务器来发送此流量。

人们一直在这样做，而且最近似乎达到了一个新的规模。 克里斯·西本曼 (Chris Siebenmann) 的理论是，“这是由一个滥用爬虫发起的大规模活动，由那些有能力在许多不同的托管提供商处获得大量服务器的人发起”，而不是一个老把戏的广泛流行。

闪电问答

问：如何验证请求是否来自真正的 Googlebot？

答：这是 Google 验证 Googlebot 的文档；简而言之，您可以使用几个“host”命令进行抽查，或者根据 Google 发布的 IP 范围进行检查。 大多数主要爬虫都会发布某种IP列表，但细节有所不同； JAFAR 提案旨在标准化这些列表，尽管它仍在通过标准制定过程。

问：如果我查找 IP 地址并发现它已注册到 Google LLC，该怎么办？

答：我仍然会执行验证过程，因为“Google LLC”也是 Google Cloud 托管 IP 地址的注册。 虽然就我个人而言，我无法找到任何最近的例子 - 如果 Google Cloud 反滥用团队有某种控制措施来打击这种情况，我不会感到惊讶。

问：我查了一下，它确实是真正的 Googlebot。 我应该怎么办？

答：请参阅 Google 的文档，了解如何处理网站的过度抓取。

问：你的意思是告诉我人们可以在互联网上撒谎？

A: Yes :(

问：如果我们添加另一个字段来阻止他们撒谎怎么办？

答：请参阅 RFC 3514，“evil bit”标准。 不幸的是，坏人不遵守这个标准。

更严肃地说，我已经为我的雇主详细撰写了有关 Web Bot Auth HTTP 签名提案的文章（与往常一样，我自己在这个博客上发表了意见）。 该提案比另一个领域稍微复杂一些，因为它涉及加密签名，但我认为这是通往“您可以信任的用户代理”的合理途径。

*问：你让我确信有些 Googlebot 是假的。 但这真的是“最”吗？

答：好吧，我承认我没有数据证明这一点。 我提出这个较弱的主张：大多数破坏性 Googlebot 流量的故事（如本文开头的引用）都是由假 Googlebot 引起的。 根据我的经验，真正的 Googlebot 表现得非常好；与此同时，假冒的 Googlebot 很乐意攻击某个网站，直到该网站爆炸。

话虽这么说，如果您看到 Googlebot 的破坏性行为（无论是真的还是假的），我很想听听 - 请通过 bobbie@digitalseams.com 联系。
